question.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-1)^{n+1}\frac{6}{n(n+2)}{x}^{n}.
$$

Find the series expansion of ${f}^{′}(x).$

${f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }$
{{field-1}}$(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n-1}$
question.worked_solution:
Writing the terms of the series explicitly, we have

$$
f(x)=2x-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+⋯+{{(-1)^{n+1}\frac{6}{n(n+2)}{x}^{n}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

Differentiating the above series term-by-term gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=2-\frac{3}{2}x+⋯+{{(-1)^{n+1}\frac{6}{n+2}{x}^{n-1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6}{n+2}(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n-1}
$$
